trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Darbhanga in Matrimonial Case No. 127 of 2011
case_name: Manorma Devi vs Sri Deep Narayan @ Vijay Panjiyar

parties.respondent_defendant: Sri Deep Narayan @ Vijay Panjiyar, husband

facts_of_case: The parties were married on 07.07.2003 and had three children. The respondent-husband filed a petition for dissolution of marriage under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, which was granted by the trial court with a decree of judicial separation under Section 10 of the Hindu Marriage Act.

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking judicial separation must make honest efforts to continue the matrimonial relationship.
legal_principles.held: The learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Darbhanga has held that the appellant-wife has not taken any honest effort to continue her matrimonial relationship with her husband, to get the matrimonial dispute settled amicably.

legal_principles.principle: A party alleging cruelty must provide specific dates and evidence to support their claims.
legal_principles.held: The respondent has alleged that his father has sustained injuries at the hands of the father and brother of the appellant but he has not produced any injury report to authenticate his claim.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed and the decree of judicial separation passed by the trial court is set aside. The parties are directed to live separately as per the terms of the decree.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act
appealing a family court judgment on dissolution of marriage
